synoptic.summary: A mid-level ridge is building over the Great Basin and stays in place through Thanksgiving. Expect dry weather, light winds and valley inversions, with patchy early-morning fog or mist. No convection is expected. Pressure at Salt Lake airport is 1028.4 mb and rising fast (up 11 mb in 23 h). A weak, splitting system adds cloud on Wednesday. Winds aloft stay light: under 12 kt from the surface up to about 5,500 ft above landing. On Thursday afternoon the flow from about 315° strengthens to 19–23 kt at around 9,500 ft above landing, ahead of a cold front that may come through late Friday into Saturday. Under this weak gradient the forecast keeps flow from 140°–160° at the Point most of each day. On Wednesday and Thursday it switches to flow from 300°–340° around 14:00. On Tuesday the forecast for the Point never switches, but the airport forecasts do.
synoptic.afd_excerpt:
Mid level ridging building into the Great Basin this
evening will become the dominant weather feature through
Thanksgiving. With this ridge in place, warmer temperatures aloft
and light winds will result likely allow valley inversions to
become established through Thanksgiving, which may allow for
patchy early morning stratus/fog.

pressure.significance: Strong high-pressure build (1017.1 mb → 1028.4 mb in 23 h at Salt Lake airport). Stable air, light gradient, and the local daily wind cycle decides which launch works. Mornings may be capped by inversion and fog.

observations.summary: Newest readings are from Monday evening, 20:55–21:30 local, so they are current at run time but about 10 h before the Tuesday morning slot. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no data. Utah Valley stations show evening flow from 310°–6° at 10–12 kt: Spanish Fork 4°/12, Alpine 2°/11, Provo 310°/10. At the gap and in the Salt Lake Valley it is nearly calm: Lehi 212°/2, Salt Lake airport 220°/3, South Valley Regional calm. The forecast has light drainage from 140°–150° by morning. The Tuesday morning airport forecasts (Salt Lake 130°–170°/3–5 kt, Provo variable 5 kt) agree with that.

d2-am.explanation: Under the ridge the wind is very light (gusts ≤ 10 kt) with nothing strong aloft, so speed is no problem. The problem is direction. The launch forecast holds 140°–150° until about 10:00, on the rotor side of the 160° cut-off, and only reaches 160° from 11:00. The airport forecast (170°) suggests it may line up earlier. If the sock shows 160°–200° it is a go; if it stays below 160°, don't launch. The evening observations are 10 h old by the slot and the Point station sent nothing, so check the sock on site.
